title: No Rock Stays Put
question: How do the three main rock types turn into one another?
hook: The same material can be igneous, then sedimentary, then metamorphic, depending on where it ends up.
idea: A rock changes type whenever its surroundings push it out of balance, so every rock is a stop on a loop rather than an end point.

beats.prompt: Put these steps in order, from a rock at the surface to new sedimentary rock.
items: Weathering breaks the rock into fragments
Natural agents carry the fragments away and deposit them
The fragments are buried and compacted
The buried fragments are lithified into rock
beats.explain: Weathering breaks rock down, the pieces are transported and deposited, then buried and compacted, and lithification turns them into sedimentary rock.

beats.prompt: Sort each into where the magma cooled.
beats.explain: Intrusive rock cools slowly within the Earth and is coarse, like granite; volcanic rock cools fast at the surface and is fine-grained or glassy, like basalt and obsidian.

beats.prompt: A slab of basalt is carried down beneath a continent as plates collide. What can happen to it?

choices.label: It stays basalt forever, since it is already igneous
choices.feedback: Tempting because basalt is already igneous, but no rock stays in equilibrium once its environment changes.

choices.label: It turns into sandstone
choices.feedback: Sandstone forms from fragments at the surface, not from rock pushed deep down.

beats.explain: Basalt subducted under a continent can melt, because rocks change when they are forced out of their equilibrium conditions.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong; which?
steps: Weathering breaks granite into grains of sand, which still count as igneous.
The sand is buried, compacted and fused into solid rock.
So the new rock must also be igneous.
beats.explain: A single grain keeps its original class, but a rock made of grains fused together is sedimentary.
